baseline: Host LTP 20260529 (/nix/store/hik6kb512ia3p14lc2vwzb292d4k306a-ltp-20260529/testcases/bin/open02) on Linux 6.8.0-124-generic: 2 passed / 0 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped. Per assertion, both at open02.c:47 via TST_EXP_FAIL2(open(...), exp_errno): (1) tcase 0, open('test_file', O_RDWR) on a name that does not exist and no O_CREAT -> returns -1 with ENOENT (2); 'TPASS: open() new file without O_CREAT : ENOENT (2)'. (2) tcase 1, setup() SAFE_TOUCHes 'test_file2' as root at mode 0644 then SAFE_SETEUIDs to nobody (65534), so the caller is a non-owner that still has read permission through the other-r bit; open('test_file2', O_RDONLY|O_NOATIME, 0444) -> returns -1 with EPERM (1); 'TPASS: open() unprivileged O_RDONLY | O_NOATIME : EPERM (1)'. The correct return is EPERM even though the ordinary DAC read check would have allowed the open, i.e. O_NOATIME is an extra privilege gate layered on top of the access-mode check, not a variant of it. Directly probed the pinned host kernel with purpose-built C programs (/tmp/noatime_probe/p.c and q.c) to pin the exact rule rather than infer it from this one observation: EPERM depends only on ownership, never on the mode bits (a root-owned 0666 file still EPERMs an O_RDONLY|O_NOATIME from nobody); the owner is exempt (nobody opening a nobody-owned 0644 file with O_NOATIME succeeds); root is exempt on files it does not own; being merely in the file's group is NOT enough (root-owned 0664 with gid=nobody still EPERM); it applies to every inode type, not just regular files (a root-owned directory EPERMs, and so does /dev/null); O_PATH is exempt (O_PATH|O_NOATIME on a root-owned file succeeds); the ordinary access-mode check runs FIRST, so O_WRONLY|O_NOATIME on a root-owned 0644 file yields EACCES (13), not EPERM, and a missing path still yields ENOENT (2) ahead of both; and fcntl(F_SETFL, O_NOATIME) is gated identically, returning EPERM and leaving the flag clear, but only on the clear->set transition (re-asserting an already-set O_NOATIME returns 0, and clearing it is always allowed).
failing_assertion: open02.c:47, tcase 1 only: 'open02.c:47: TFAIL: open() unprivileged O_RDONLY | O_NOATIME succeeded'. Asterinas returns a valid file descriptor (open() >= 0, success) where Linux returns -1/EPERM; TST_EXP_FAIL2 reports TFAIL because the call did not fail at all, so there is no wrong errno, the error is simply never raised. Run result 1 passed / 1 failed / 0 broken / 0 skipped versus host 2/2; tcase 0 is green ('TPASS: open() new file without O_CREAT : ENOENT (2)'), confirming select.json's prediction that only the second subtest is at fault. Captured by temporarily adding --verbose to test/initramfs/src/conformance/ltp/run_ltp_test.sh, since the default kirk output only prints 'open02: fail'; that scaffolding edit has been reverted and the worktree is clean. Asterinas ran the test on ramfs (CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR=/tmp), the host on overlayfs.
root_cause: O_NOATIME is parsed and stored but never authorized. StatusFlags::O_NOATIME (kernel/src/fs/file/file_attr/status_flags.rs:22) is a plain bitflag; OpenArgs::from_flags_and_mode (kernel/src/fs/file/file_attr/open_args.rs:19-57) builds status_flags with StatusFlags::from_bits_truncate(flags) and validates only the O_TMPFILE and O_CREAT|O_DIRECTORY combinations, so O_NOATIME passes through untouched. sys_openat -> do_open (kernel/src/syscall/open.rs:80-128) hands those flags to Path::open (kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/mod.rs:124-163), which tests O_CREAT|O_EXCL, O_CREAT-on-dir, O_NOFOLLOW-on-symlink, O_DIRECTORY and O_TRUNC and then calls InodeHandle::new (kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs:40-50). InodeHandle::new performs exactly one credential test, inode.check_permission(access_mode.into()) at line 46, which is the access-mode DAC check; for a 0644 root-owned file opened O_RDONLY by fsuid 65534 that check passes through the other-r branch of Inode::check_permission (kernel/src/fs/vfs/fs_apis/inode.rs:573+). Nothing anywhere then compares the caller's fsuid against the inode's uid on account of O_NOATIME: grepping NOATIME across kernel/ and ostd/ returns only this bitflag definition, its two mask memberships (StatusFlags::SETFL_MASK at status_flags.rs:35 and SettableStatusFlags::minimal at status_flags.rs:51), and unrelated mount-flag plumbing (vfs/path/mount.rs:151,175,214,664-672; syscall/fsmount.rs:61,105-114; syscall/mount.rs:264; syscall/statfs.rs:133) - never a credential test. So the flag is simply recorded into FileCommon::new(path, status_flags) at inode_handle.rs:69 and open() succeeds. The absent check is a whole missing step, not a miscoded one.
invariant: Requesting O_NOATIME on a file description requires that the caller own the underlying inode (fsuid equal to the inode's uid) or hold CAP_FOWNER; otherwise the request must fail with EPERM. The rule is independent of the file's permission bits and of its inode type, and it is evaluated after the access-mode permission check (so EACCES from an unreadable/unwritable file, and ENOENT from a missing path, take precedence over EPERM). It applies both when the flag is requested at open time and when it is newly asserted on an existing description, but not when the flag is already set or is being cleared. O_PATH descriptions, which carry no I/O rights at all, are exempt.
owning_layer: The VFS open-permission step, above every filesystem: concretely InodeHandle::new in kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs:40-50, immediately after the existing inode.check_permission call at line 46 and inside the existing !O_PATH guard at line 42. That is Asterinas's structural equivalent of the tail of Linux's may_open(), and the placement is forced by the ordering requirement - the check must sit after the access-mode DAC test to keep EACCES ahead of EPERM, and Path::open (vfs/path/mod.rs:124-163) is the closer analogue of may_open() by content but runs entirely before that test, so putting it there would invert the two errnos and contradict the host probe. The !O_PATH guard already in place at line 42 delivers the O_PATH exemption for free, matching Linux exactly. The second, independent site is the F_SETFL entry path, handle_setfl in kernel/src/syscall/fcntl.rs:87-95. This must not go into any filesystem: ramfs, ext2, exfat, virtiofs and the pseudo filesystems would each need the same rule, and only the first is exercised by this test.
linux_reference: Read Linux v6.8 sources fetched directly (fs/namei.c, fs/fcntl.c, fs/open.c, fs/inode.c). The rule is enforced in may_open(), fs/namei.c:3286-3288: '/* O_NOATIME can only be set by the owner or superuser */ if (flag & O_NOATIME && !inode_owner_or_capable(idmap, inode)) return -EPERM;'. It is the last test in may_open(), placed deliberately after 'error = inode_permission(idmap, inode, MAY_OPEN | acc_mode);' (fs/namei.c:3272-3274), which is what makes EACCES outrank EPERM. Note this is NOT in do_dentry_open()/fs/open.c on any current kernel - v6.8's fs/open.c contains no reference to O_NOATIME at all (it lived there only on much older kernels), correcting select.json's rationale on that point; the layer conclusion is unaffected since both are VFS above the filesystem. inode_owner_or_capable() (fs/inode.c) is 'i_uid == current_fsuid() || ns_capable(ns, CAP_FOWNER)', which is precisely the shape Asterinas already open-codes twice: Dentry::check_sticky_bit_permission (kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/dentry.rs:471-489) and Path::check_hardlink_source (kernel/src/fs/vfs/path/mod.rs:272-323) both compare posix_thread.credentials().fsuid() against metadata.uid and fall back to lsm_hooks::on_capable(CapableContext::new(UserNamespace::get_init_singleton().as_ref(), posix_thread, CapSet::FOWNER)). may_open() is reached from do_open() at fs/namei.c:3643 on every ordinary open and from do_tmpfile() at fs/namei.c:3701 for O_TMPFILE, in both cases including newly created files (FMODE_CREATED zeroes acc_mode but leaves open_flag, so the O_NOATIME test still runs); do_o_path() never calls may_open() at all, which is why O_PATH is exempt. F_SETFL is gated separately in setfl(), fs/fcntl.c:49-52, guarded by '(arg & O_NOATIME) && !(filp->f_flags & O_NOATIME)' so only the clear->set transition is charged, and O_NOATIME is in that file's SETFL_MASK at fs/fcntl.c:35 exactly as it is in Asterinas's StatusFlags::SETFL_MASK.
other_callers: Two user-reachable ways to assert O_NOATIME exist, and both are unguarded. (1) open/openat/creat via sys_openat -> do_open (kernel/src/syscall/open.rs:21-128); creat cannot express O_NOATIME because it hardcodes its flags at open.rs:75-76, and there is no openat2 in the tree (zero hits for openat2/open_how), so this reduces to the single Path::open -> InodeHandle::new path the test exercises. (2) fcntl(F_SETFL) -> handle_setfl (kernel/src/syscall/fcntl.rs:87-95), which calls file.update_status_flags(StatusFlagsUpdate::replace(new_flags)) with no credential test whatsoever; because O_NOATIME is a member of StatusFlags::SETFL_MASK (status_flags.rs:35) and of SettableStatusFlags::minimal (status_flags.rs:51), which every file type includes, an unprivileged caller can acquire O_NOATIME on any already-open fd on any file type. The host probe confirms Linux returns EPERM there and leaves the flag clear, so this is the same defect reachable through a second syscall and it is why the rule belongs to the layer rather than to open(). Fixing only InodeHandle::new leaves it live; open02 would still pass. The other two open flavours in do_open, the O_CREAT-new-file branch (open.rs:119-123) and O_TMPFILE (open.rs:151-155), bypass InodeHandle::new by calling new_unchecked_access directly, so a fix placed in InodeHandle::new will not cover them - that is harmless and matches Linux behaviourally, because a freshly created inode takes uid from the creator's fsuid (ramfs current_fs_ids at kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ramfs/fs.rs:1453-1461, used at 897/945/982), so the caller is by construction the owner and inode_owner_or_capable would always succeed. The remaining in-kernel InodeHandle constructions cannot carry a user-supplied O_NOATIME and are unaffected: nsfs.rs:278, ramfs/memfd.rs:274 and pipe/anon_pipe.rs:32-34 pass StatusFlags::empty() or internally chosen flags, fs/mod.rs:42-65 builds stdin/stdout/stderr from OpenArgs::from_modes (which hardcodes status_flags to empty, open_args.rs:60-67), and device/pty/master.rs:203 likewise uses OpenArgs::from_modes. Separately and out of scope for this test: O_NOATIME has no semantic effect in Asterinas even once granted, because atime is updated inside the filesystems with no consultation of the flag (ext2 kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ext2/inode/file.rs:35,82 and ramfs kernel/src/fs/fs_impls/ramfs/fs.rs:716,771), and the per-mount AtimePolicy in vfs/path/mount.rs:171-217 is likewise never consulted on a read; open02 only asserts the EPERM gate, so suppressing atime updates is a genuine but separate gap that should not be folded into this fix.
suggested_direction: Add the owner-or-CAP_FOWNER test as a new step in the VFS open-permission path, then repeat it on the F_SETFL transition. First, factor the duplicated idiom into one helper - Dentry::check_sticky_bit_permission (vfs/path/dentry.rs:471-489) and Path::check_hardlink_source (vfs/path/mod.rs:272-323) already implement inode_owner_or_capable twice - ideally as a method beside Inode::check_permission in kernel/src/fs/vfs/fs_apis/inode.rs, mirroring how check_permission short-circuits to Ok(()) when there is no current task or no posix_thread (inode.rs:573-579) so kernel-internal opens during boot keep working. Then in InodeHandle::new (kernel/src/fs/file/inode_handle.rs:40-50), inside the existing !O_PATH branch and strictly AFTER the inode.check_permission(access_mode.into())? at line 46, add: if status_flags.contains(StatusFlags::O_NOATIME) then require owner-or-CAP_FOWNER on path.inode(), else return EPERM. Ordering is load-bearing: placing it before line 46, or in Path::open, turns the O_WRONLY|O_NOATIME-on-an-unwritable-file case from EACCES into EPERM. Do not add it to new_unchecked_access - the creator owns the new inode so it would be dead code there, and it would wrongly apply to the internal pipe/memfd/nsfs constructions. Second, in handle_setfl (kernel/src/syscall/fcntl.rs:87-95), apply the same test only on the clear->set transition, i.e. when the requested flags contain O_NOATIME and the file's current status flags do not; re-asserting an already-set flag and clearing it must both keep returning 0, and on EPERM the flag must be left unchanged rather than partially applied, which means checking before the update_status_flags call. Regression traps, all confirmed against the host: the owner must still succeed; root on a file it does not own must still succeed (so CAP_FOWNER, not a uid==0 test); group membership must NOT be sufficient; mode bits must not influence the outcome; O_PATH|O_NOATIME must keep succeeding; a nonexistent path must still give ENOENT ahead of EPERM; and the rule must hold for directories and device nodes, not just regular files. Since the LTP run uses CONFORMANCE_TEST_WORKDIR=/tmp the target filesystem is ramfs, but placing the check above the filesystem is what keeps ext2/exfat/virtiofs consistent for free.
